findings.summary: The requirements wave now depends on review-mode provenance, but no shared upstream requirement defines the canonical field or vocabulary for `review_mode` across manual and runtime evidence.
findings.rationale: Evaluation Requirement 9, Self-Improvement Requirement 7, and Paper-Interface Requirement 6 all require review-mode distinction, yet foundation metadata and runtime requirements do not define where this provenance lives or how it is normalized. This creates a cross-feature contract gap before design.
findings.suggested_action: Add an upstream contract for review-mode provenance, likely in foundation metadata contract and possibly runtime evidence requirements, with a canonical vocabulary that downstream features can reuse.
findings.decision_note: Accepted and reflected by adding review-mode provenance contract to foundation/runtime plus downstream provenance consumers.

findings.summary: The requirements do not yet define the handoff rule that decides when manual dogfooding evidence stops being primary and runtime-mediated evidence becomes the standard comparison population.
findings.rationale: Intent now distinguishes Phase 1 manual dogfooding from later runtime-mediated evidence, but the requirements wave does not yet specify which feature owns the transition rule or how mixed populations should be constrained before comparison and proposal generation.

affected_refs.section: 12.5 本 repo への手動適用

findings.suggested_action: Define which requirement set owns the handoff boundary and whether the rule is metadata-based, protocol-based, or workflow-based before design proceeds.
findings.decision_note: Accepted and reflected by assigning standard comparison-population ownership to evaluation and documenting operational handling in invalidation policy.
